stories.snippet: A jury trial is scheduled to begin March 29, following a hearing Monday with Clancy’s defense attorneys and prosecutors.

digest.text: Clancy’s first trial on charges of first-degree murder ended in mistrial after jurors couldn’t reach unanimous verdict.
The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

stories.snippet: The U.S. aviation regulator said the communications outage was caused by failures in the country's aging air traffic control infrastructure.

digest.text: The airline ground stop that wreaked havoc on travel since Friday was not related to the FAA’s new, $875 million AI-powered system the agency is rolling out to help predict problems in the sky, according to government officials and the artificial intelligence company behind the technology.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued the clarification in a question-and-answer update after speculation over whether the outage was linked to the recently launched Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) system.

stories.headline: Schumer vs. Van Hollen: Who has the edge?
stories.snippet: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (N.Y.) is facing a challenge for his job from the left in Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) The leadership battle comes after Democrats won sweeping victories in the midterm elections and highlights division in the party despite the big wins.

digest.text: US Sen. Chris Van Hollen said Sunday that around 15 fellow Senate Democrats have backed his bid to lead the caucus in the new Congress and accused Sen. Chuck Schumer—the current Democratic leader—of falsely painting his effort to remain in charge as a foregone conclusion.

Sanders made the case for replacing Schumer in a video released Monday, casting the January 2027 leadership contest as a broader debate over the Democratic Party’s future rather than a personal dispute between the two senators.

Van Hollen disputed a list of committed votes reportedly shared by Schumer’s team, saying, “I can tell you that a number of those people on that list have actually committed to voting for me, and the others are very open to the idea of change.”
Van Hollen began his political career as a protégé of Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) but has moved toward the progressive camp in recent years.
